# 佛說解節經

**ID:** T0677
**Volume:** T16
**Category:** 經集部類
**Original Category:** 經集部
**Byline:** 陳 真諦譯
**Dynasty:** 陳
**Date:** 558–569
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0677

## Contributors
- 真諦 (A000962)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T677 in one fascicle is [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) / Paramārtha's partial translation of the *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra*, covering only the second chapter of the parent sūtra (the *Paramārtha-lakṣaṇa-parivarta* 勝義諦相品 / *prabhāvitalakṣaṇa* — the chapter on the Mark of Ultimate Truth). Translated under the Chén 陳 dynasty in the southern capital, between [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6)'s settled period at Jiànkāng / Guǎngzhōu (557–569). Aligned with chapter T16N0676-2 / *Shèngyìdì xiāng pǐn* of [玄奘's full version](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0353).

**Abstract**

The *Jiějié jīng* is one of three "extract" Chinese translations of individual chapters of the *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra* — the others being [KR6i0356](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0356) (T678 by [Guṇabhadra](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%82%E9%82%A3%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85), partial of chapter 7) and [KR6i0357](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0357) (T679 by [Guṇabhadra](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B1%82%E9%82%A3%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80%E7%BE%85), partial of chapter 8). Although the title may suggest a freestanding sūtra, the text is in fact a partial witness of the same parent translated more comprehensively by [Bodhiruci](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) in 514 ([KR6i0352](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0352) / T675) and definitively by [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) in 647 ([KR6i0353](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0353) / T676). [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) (499–569) — the Yogācāra translator-patriarch who reached Liáng China in 546 and worked under increasingly precarious conditions through the late Liáng and early Chén dynasties until his death in 569 — translated this small chapter likely between 557 (the founding of the Chén) and 569 (his death). The single-fascicle translation is brief but historically important: it shows that the *Saṃdhinirmocana* was already in the corpus that [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) brought south, and that the sūtra was being read piece-by-piece in the southern Yogācāra circle that would eventually produce the *She lùn* 攝論 (*Mahāyāna-saṃgraha*) school.

The *Jiějié* version's terminology differs significantly from [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s standard Yogācāra vocabulary; for example, [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6)'s renderings of the three self-natures and the three turnings of the wheel use older, less consistent Chinese equivalents. For that reason the text is a key witness for early-sixth-century pre-Xuánzàng Chinese Yogācāra terminology.

Related canonical recensions: complete versions [KR6i0352](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0352) (T675 by Bodhiruci); [KR6i0353](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0353) (T676 by Xuánzàng); other partial extracts [KR6i0356](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0356) (T678) and [KR6i0357](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0357) (T679); commentary on the parent [KR6i0354](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0354) (X369 by Wǒnch'ǔk).
